chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Checking whom he arranged for: Dorsey, Hines, Lunceford, Red Allen
summary: He did not arrange for Casa Loma, Tommy Dorsey or Earl Hines; he did for Jimmy Dorsey, wrote 'Jeep Rhythm' for Jimmie Lunceford during the war, and recorded with Red Allen.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: : Yeah. Well, I'll tell you what, time being what it is, why don't we call it quits. But I'm intending to do on some of the next sessions is get down to some details about various people we have all ready, like with Hawkins and so on. But there's some others I'd like to talk about, and we'll, from time to time, get back into just some of the musical things, and also, I want to spend some time -- I've got it here from various lists I've acquired, that you -- and we've already talked about some of this -- that you arranged of course for Fletcher, some times, for Benny Goodman, Charley Barnet, and one account said you arranged for the Casa Loma Orchestra. Is that correct?
That's incorrect. I did something for Jimmy Dorsey.
: Yeah, I've got Tommy Dorsey here. Not Tommy?
And Earl Hines? Did you do any arranging for him?
No. I didn't do anything for Earl.
Okay, then we'll knock that out. How about Jimmy Lunceford, cause that's down too.
Oh yes. I did a tune during the war called 'Jeep Rhythm' that I'm still drawing royalties off.
Okay. Well, we'll talk about that. And Red Allen?
Oh yeah. We recorded a lot of things.
